fr.title: A propos de nous
fr.description: Bienvenue dans le monde de Magical Steps Travel ! Nous sommes une agence de voyages agréée créée en 1993, située à Kusadasi, en Turquie, spécialisée dans les circuits d'Ephèse, les circuits d'Istanbul, les circuits de Cappadoce, les circuit
fr.bodyHtml:
Bienvenue dans le monde de Magical Steps Travel !

Nous sommes une agence de voyages agréée créée en 1993, située à Kusadasi, en Turquie, spécialisée dans les circuits d'Ephèse, les circuits d'Istanbul, les circuits de Cappadoce, les circuits de Pamukkale, les circuits culturels, religieux et privés dans toute la Turquie.  En tant qu'agent de voyage compétent, nous vous invitons à explorer la nature mystique et fascinante de la Turquie.  Étant le carrefour et le berceau des civilisations, l'Asie Mineure offre beaucoup d'histoire, de culture et de beauté naturelle.  Non seulement son patrimoine historique, mais aussi des gens colorés et des plus sympathiques vous attendent.

Notre équipe expérimentée s'est réunie pour vous assurer de recevoir les meilleurs guides touristiques, hébergement et transport.  Nous vous offrons la flexibilité de choisir le meilleur circuit pour vous-même en fonction de vos intérêts, besoins et attentes.

Magical Steps Travel organise des visites de petits et grands groupes.  Des visites de groupe préparées par des professionnels vous offrent diverses sélections touristiques du pays et des habitants.

Les visites d'Éphèse au départ de Kusadasi, du port/de l'aéroport d'Izmir/de l'hôtel ou d'Istanbul sont fournies par des guides touristiques d'Éphèse privés, professionnels, expérimentés, agréés et locaux qui ont d'excellentes critiques sur TripAdvisor.  Cliquez pour lire nos avis sur TripAdvisor.  Nous organisons des visites privées d'Ephèse comprenant les frais d'entrée, le parking, le déjeuner, un guide privé, les transferts privés, l'essence et le gaz.  Il n'y a pas de frais cachés ni de frais supplémentaires facturés à la date de la visite.  Découvrez également nos autres circuits au départ de Kusadasi et les circuits au départ d'Izmir

Des visites d'Istanbul depuis le port et l'hôtel sont proposées par des guides touristiques privés d'Istanbul, agréés et expérimentés.  Vous serez pris en charge au port ou à l'hôtel d'Istanbul par votre guide et vous reviendrez à la fin de la visite.  Nous pouvons personnaliser le meilleur itinéraire d'Istanbul pour vous en fonction de votre séjour à Istanbul et de vos intérêts.  Cliquez ici pour notre page de visites d'Istanbul.

Nous proposons également des circuits en Cappadoce au départ d'Istanbul.  Il existe des options de visite de 3 jours et une balade en montgolfière en Cappadoce peut être ajoutée à votre itinéraire.  Si vous le souhaitez, nous pouvons également organiser pour vous des visites de la Cappadoce et d'Éphèse au départ d'Istanbul.

Si vous avez des questions, n'hésitez pas à nous contacter via le formulaire de contact.  Cliquez ici pour le formulaire de contact.

Magical Steps est membre de TURSAB (Association des agences de voyages turques / Ministère turc de la culture et du tourisme) Le nom de la licence est : Family Turizm.  Numéro : 2511. (Family Tour appartient à Magical Steps Travel LLC) et membre de KUTO (Kusadasi Chamber of Commerce) Numéro de membre : 5569

de.bodyHtml:
Willkommen in der Welt von Magical Steps Travel!

Wir sind ein lizenziertes Reisebüro, das 1993 in Kusadasi, Türkei, gegründet wurde und sich auf Ephesus-Touren, Istanbul-Touren, Kappadokien-Touren, Pamukkale-Touren, kulturelle, religiöse und private Touren in der ganzen Türkei spezialisiert hat. Als kompetenter Reisevermittler laden wir Sie ein, die mystische und faszinierende Natur der Türkei zu erkunden. Als Kreuzung und Wiege der Zivilisationen bietet Kleinasien viel Geschichte, Kultur und natürliche Schönheit. Nicht nur ihr historisches Erbe, sondern auch bunte und freundliche Menschen erwarten Sie.

Unser erfahrenes Team ist zusammengekommen, um sicherzustellen, dass Sie die besten Reiseleiter, Unterkünfte und Transportmöglichkeiten erhalten. Wir bieten Ihnen die Flexibilität, die für Sie beste Tour entsprechend Ihren Interessen, Bedürfnissen und Erwartungen auszuwählen.

Magical Steps Travel organisiert kleine und große Gruppenreisen. Professionell vorbereitete Gruppenreisen bieten Ihnen verschiedene Sehenswürdigkeiten zu Land und Leuten.

Ephesus-Touren von Kusadasi, dem Hafen von Izmir/Flughafen/Hotel oder Istanbul werden von privaten, professionellen, erfahrenen, lizenzierten, lokalen Ephesus-Reiseleitern angeboten, die großartige Bewertungen auf TripAdvisor haben. Klicken Sie hier, um unsere Bewertungen auf TripAdvisor zu lesen. Wir arrangieren private Ephesus-Touren einschließlich Eintrittsgebühren, Parkplatz, Mittagessen, privatem Reiseleiter, privatem Transfer, Benzin und Benzin. Es gibt keine versteckten Gebühren und Zusatzkosten, die Ihnen am Tourdatum in Rechnung gestellt werden. Sehen Sie sich auch unsere anderen Touren ab Kusadasi und Touren ab Izmir an

Istanbul-Touren vom Hafen und vom Hotel werden von privaten Istanbul-Reiseleitern angeboten, die lizenziert und erfahren sind. Sie werden von Ihrem Reiseleiter vom Hafen oder Hotel in Istanbul abgeholt und am Ende der Tour wieder zurückgebracht. Wir können die beste Istanbul-Reiseroute für Sie entsprechend Ihrer Zeit in Istanbul und Ihren Interessen anpassen. Klicken Sie hier für unsere Istanbul-Touren-Seite.

Wir bieten auch Kappadokien-Touren ab Istanbul an. Es gibt 3-tägige Touroptionen und eine Ballonfahrt in Kappadokien kann zu Ihrer Reiseroute hinzugefügt werden. Auf Wunsch organisieren wir für Sie auch Kappadokien- und Ephesus-Touren ab Istanbul.

Bei Fragen können Sie uns gerne per Kontaktformular kontaktieren. Klicken Sie hier, um das Kontaktformular anzuzeigen.

Magical Steps ist ein Mitglied von TURSAB (Verband türkischer Reisebüros / türkisches Ministerium für Kultur und Tourismus). Der Lizenzname lautet: Family Turizm. Nummer: 2511. en.title: Hadrian`s Temple
en.description: It is one of the Roman Emperor Temples. Hadrian the Emperor of Rome visited Ephesus twice. Such a beautiful Temple was built honor of him in the 2nd Century AD. Hadrian’s Temple is one of the best ruins in Ephesus and was restored recently.
en.bodyHtml:
It is one of the Roman Emperor Temples. Hadrian the Emperor of Rome visited Ephesus twice. Such a beautiful Temple was built honor of him in the 2nd Century AD. Hadrian’s Temple is one of the best ruins in Ephesus and was restored recently. The Hadrian’s Temple was converted into a Christian church in the 4th Century AD.

There are great friezes on the temple displaying a wonderful craftsmanship. The bust of Tyche is visible on the arch. Tyche is the goddess of fortune that’s why her Roman name is Fortune. Inside the frieze Medusa is visible. Also other friezes are telling about the Amazons, Androklos and the Imperial family which are visible. The last mentioned ones are pilasters and the originals are in the Museum in Ephesus/Selcuk. In front of the temple there are four basements. There were statues of Roman Emperor on each of them.

en.title: Isis Temple
en.description: It is an Egyptian Temple located in the government agora. It was dedicated to the Egypt Goddess Isis. Later in Roman time, it was dedicated to the Roman Emperor Augustus. This was the first temple dedicated to an Egyptian goddess. There is
en.bodyHtml:
It is an Egyptian Temple located in the government agora. It was dedicated to the Egypt Goddess Isis. Later in Roman time, it was dedicated to the Roman Emperor Augustus. This was the first temple dedicated to an Egyptian goddess.

There is another temple dedicated to an Egyptian goddess named Serapes Temple. There was always a good relationship between Ephesus and Egypt in the ancient times. There were some Egyptian businessmen living in Ephesus. That’s why Egyptian temple were built in Ephesus.

en.title: The Fountain of Pollio
en.description: It is one of the many monumental fountains in Ephesus. It was dedicated to the city by the rich Roman Pollios Sextiliues. This fountain was build and dedicated to Roman Emperor Domitian. It is just opposite the temple of Domitian. Nowadays
en.bodyHtml:
It is one of the many monumental fountains in Ephesus. It was dedicated to the city by the rich Roman Pollios Sextiliues. This fountain was build and dedicated to Roman Emperor Domitian. It is just opposite the temple of Domitian.

Nowadays a restoration will start in this foundation. The arch was restored a few years ago; the mythological group of Odysseus and the Polyphemus were depicted. Some relics are in the Museum of Ephesus/Selcuk. The fountain was built in the 1st Century AD.

en.title: Hercules Gate
en.description: Hercules Gate is located at the beginning of Curetes street. Heracles' relics are visible on the two columns. It is a gate dividing the upper city of Ephesus. On this gate the frieze of Goddess Nicephorus (Roman Victoria) was situated. In t
en.bodyHtml:
Hercules Gate is located at the beginning of Curetes street. Heracles' relics are visible on the two columns. It is a gate dividing the upper city of Ephesus. On this gate the frieze of Goddess Nicephorus (Roman Victoria) was situated.

In the mythology Hercules (Heracles) hunted a lion named Nemea. That’s why Hercules is depicted with a lion head on his body and also he is wrapped into the lion fell. These two pillars which are representing Hercules from the 2nd Century. But we know that this gate was erected on the 5th Century. That means in the ancient time they removed these two pillars from somewhere else in the city to this location and used them here to build the gate.

en.title: Commercial Agora
en.description: It is one of the two Agoras located in Ephesus with 11,000sqm of size. There were shops on 4 sides of the Agora. It was built on the Hellenistic period and enlarged on the Roman period. It was the biggest shopping area on that period. St Pa
en.bodyHtml:
It is one of the two Agoras located in Ephesus with 11,000sqm of size. There were shops on 4 sides of the Agora. It was built on the Hellenistic period and enlarged on the Roman period. It was the biggest shopping area on that period. St Paul worked as a tent maker in the Commercial Agora with Priscilla and Aquila.

In the Hellenistic time the Commercial Agora of Ephesus was open only one day of the week.In the Roman Period the Agora was open every day. It was very close to the port and there was a direct connection to the Harbour Street. On four sides there were columned galleries and the floor was paved with mosaics. The center of the Agora was uncovered and paved with marble slabs. There was the Serapis Temple at the north of the Agora. This temple is the second Egyptian temple in Ephesus.

en.title: Prytaneion
en.description: Prytaneon is the place where the holly fire was. The names of the monks and nuns who took a duty here in this place are written on the 2 columns. It was dedicated to the Goddess of Fire Hestia and was the holly center of the city. Two big o
en.bodyHtml:
Prytaneon is the place where the holly fire was. The names of the monks and nuns who took a duty here in this place are written on the 2 columns. It was dedicated to the Goddess of Fire Hestia and was the holly center of the city.

Two big original Artemis monuments were found in the excavations in Prytaneon and visible in Ephesus Museum.

en.title: Temple of Domitian
en.description: It is the biggest Temple that was built in the city center. It was built for the Roman Emperor Domitian on the 3 floor podium. A huge head and left arm of a Domitian Monument is visible in the Ephesus Museum. The podium of the temple was hu
en.bodyHtml:
It is the biggest Temple that was built in the city center. It was built for the Roman Emperor Domitian on the 3 floor podium. A huge head and left arm of a Domitian Monument is visible in the Ephesus Museum. The podium of the temple was huge and measured 100 meters by 50 meter.

On the second storey figures of soldiers and priestess were depicted. There was an altar in front of the temple. Domitian was known as an emperor who harmed and pursuit Christians. Before the temple was completed, a servant killed Domitian. That’s why the temple was also dedicated to Vespasianus who became the new emperor. Later, Christians destroyed the foundation.

en.title: The Great Theatre
en.description: It is the biggest ancient theater in Turkey with a capacity of 24.000 seats. It was built 4th Century BC. It took 60 years to build this huge Theater of Ephesus. It was a Greek Theater which had been converted into a Roman Theatre. There wa
en.bodyHtml:
It is the biggest ancient theater in Turkey with a capacity of 24.000 seats. It was built 4th Century BC.  It took 60 years to build this huge Theater of Ephesus. It was a Greek Theater which had been converted into a Roman Theatre. There was a three storied stage building, erected in different times and paid by different Roman Emperor.

The Stage was added in the Roman Period. The drainage for rainwater is still visible. This Theater is also the place where St. Paul was protested by the Silversmith Demetrius and his friends. There was a big demonstration against him as he was against Goddess Artemis. Today this Theater is also famous for modern events and concerts. Popular singers such as Elton John, Chris de Burg, Lionel Richie, Joan Baez, Julio Elyases, Pavarotti, Sting and Madonna gave concerts in this Theater of Ephesus.

en.title: Public Toilets
en.description: These were the only public toilets in Ephesus and it is said that they were for man. Toilets are very well protected. There should be another public toilet for women in Ephesus which hasn't been found yet. There were 44 holes on the three s
en.bodyHtml:
These were the only public toilets in Ephesus and it is said that they were for man. Toilets are very well protected. There should be another public toilet for women in Ephesus which hasn't been found yet.

There were 44 holes on the three sides of Ephesus. There was a fresh water channel just in front of the holes. There were mosaic paved floors. There was an open-air pool in the center. People had to pay entrance fees to the public toilets.

en.title: Marble Street
en.description: It is one of the main streets of Ephesus. It starts in front of Celsus Library, passes Theatre and reaches to the Temple of Artemis. The Library and the Agora are on the right side of the Marble street. Brothel is on the left side of the st
en.bodyHtml:
It is one of the main streets of Ephesus. It starts in front of Celsus Library, passes Theatre and reaches to the Temple of Artemis. The Library and the Agora are on the right side of the Marble street. Brothel is on the left side of the street. Further on the right there is the theater and further to its left there is a gymnasium. It also cuts the Port Street.

There is marble pavement, reserved for chariots in the middle of the street is. On the right there is a covered gallery area carried by marble columns for pedestrians just behind the stores. On the left there is on a podium a side walk for pedestrian, which was also covered. This was a gift of the Roman Emperor Nero to Ephesus.

en.title: Scholastica Baths
en.description: It was a beautiful Roman Bath complex located in the centrum along the Curetes Street, Ephesus. It was restored by a rich Christian woman named Scholastica after the earthquake in the 4th Century. There is a statue of Scholastica in the bat
en.bodyHtml:
It was a beautiful Roman Bath complex located in the centrum along the Curetes Street, Ephesus.  It was restored by a rich Christian woman named Scholastica after the earthquake in the 4th Century. There is a statue of Scholastica in the bath. Every room of the bath can be seen.

This Bath had four sections. The first section was called Apotheterium which was the dressing room. The second section was called Frigidarium which was the cold water bath. The third room was the Tepidarium which was the section of lukewarm water. The last section was named Caldarium which was the hot section of the bath complex. In the Tepidarium there were a basement and bronze statues of Donaters on the basements. The Scholastica Bath is in the center of Ephesus facing the Terrace Houses.

en.title: State Agora
en.description: It is the second agora in Ephesus. It is the government Agora. Political subjects were discussed here and it was open to public. Women and the slaves could attend the meetings here. Isis temple and an altar were built inside the Agora. It w
en.bodyHtml:
It is the second agora in Ephesus. It is the government Agora. Political subjects were discussed here and it was open to public. Women and the slaves could attend the meetings here.

Isis temple and an altar were built inside the Agora. It was built in a 6.000sqm are without a roof. But four sides were covered by marble column galleries. This structure was converted into a Forum in Roman period. It collapsed in the earthquake which destroyed Ephesus in the 7th Century AD. The temple of Isis was converted and dedicated to the Roman Emperor Augustus.

en.title: Harbor Street
en.description: It is one of the three main streets of Ephesus. Harbor Street starts from the theater and end at the harbor. It is 530meters long and there were shops and crosswalks on both sides. This street is also called “Arcadian” and it is about 11 me
en.bodyHtml:
It is one of the three main streets of Ephesus. Harbor Street starts from the theater and end at the harbor. It is 530meters long and there were shops and crosswalks on both sides. This street is also called “Arcadian” and it is about 11 meters wide. It was very close to the harbour and there was 'Four Columned Monument' at the end of the street.

On each of these columns the statues of the four Evangelists was situated. This street is also known to be lightened at nights. Holes were made on the columns in order to put torches in it. The Gymnasium takes place on the right of this main street. This was the high school of Ephesus. Next to the harbour there was a huge Roman Bath. Near the Roman Bath there is the Church of Virgin Mary, which was built as a pagan high school but converted into a Church in the 4th Century AD. It is the first church ever named after the Mother of Jesus Christ. This Church is also called Ecumenical Council Church because the 3rd Council held in this structure in 431 AD in Ephesus.

en.title: The Mosaic - Paved sidewalk
en.description: This was the area for the pedestrians which belongs to the 5th - 6th centuries. These mosaics are located in front of the Terrace Houses. At the Curetes Street which was one of the main streets of Ephesus, there were paths on the each side.
en.bodyHtml:
This was the area for the pedestrians which belongs to the 5th - 6th centuries. These mosaics are located in front of the Terrace Houses. At the Curetes Street which was one of the main streets of Ephesus, there were paths on the each side.

In the middle there was a marble paved main road for chariots. Behind the sidewalks there were stores on both sides and finally the terrace houses on the slopes. The Mosaics on the side walks are displaying a great workmanship.

en.title: Gate of Mazeus and Mithridates
en.description: This gate is located next to the Celsus Library and opens to Agora. It was built by the slaves Mazeus and Mithridates 2000 year ago for Roman Emperor Augustus. Mazues and Mithridates were both architects.Then they became slaves of the imper
en.bodyHtml:
This gate is located next to the Celsus Library and opens to Agora. It was built by the slaves Mazeus and Mithridates 2000 year ago for Roman Emperor Augustus. Mazues and Mithridates were both architects.Then they became slaves of the imperial family of Augustus.

After being emancipated, they built and dedicated this gate to Augustus, to his wife Livia, to Julia and Marcus Agrippa. The inscription is carved by cupper and is written with Latin letters. This structure has been restored. The Inscription is original.

en.title: Baths of Varius
en.description: It was built by the rich Roman Varius for the Ephesians and located on the upper Ephesus. This bath was built in the 1st century AD and was destroyed in the 7th Century AD. The bath was next to many public buildings so Ephesians were visiti
en.bodyHtml:
It was built by the rich Roman Varius for the Ephesians and located on the upper Ephesus. This bath was built in the 1st century AD and was destroyed in the 7th Century AD.

The bath was next to many public buildings so Ephesians were visiting this bath after meetings people. It was also very close to the Magnesian Gate of Ephesus. People could have bath and rest here before they entered Ephesus, having a long travel. In the Roman bath they had certain heating system. This was a kind of a floor heating system invented by the Romans called Hypocaust.

en.title: Library of Celsus
en.description: Library of Celsus is one of the symbols of Ephesus. It was built by Aquila for the famous governor Celsus as a monument and library. It is the third largest library in the ancient times. It is said that there were 12.000 papyrus rolls in Ce
en.bodyHtml:
Library of Celsus is one of the symbols of Ephesus. It was built by Aquila for the famous governor Celsus as a monument and library. It is the third largest library in the ancient times. It is said that there were 12.000 papyrus rolls in Celsus Library. It was destroyed in an earthquake and was rebuilt according to the original on the restorations held between 1970 and 1978.

Celsus Library is the first example of a Grave Monument-Library. After a short time the second one was built in Sagalassos. The tomb of Celsus is under the central niche of the library. In the 3rd Century AD Goths burnt the library. In the 11th Century AD an earthquake destroyed the structure. The copies of the four women statues are visible today. Originals are in the museum of Vienna. In the second story there are basements. On each of these basements three bronze statues of Celsus and one statue of Aquila were situated. Both Celsus and his son were Proconsuls of Ephesus. But they are not found. Faces of Medusa who is related to death can be seen on the top of the Library.

en.title: Odeon
en.description: It is located on the upper Ephesus and built by Romans. The Odeon is well-preserved with a capacity of 1400 seats. It was used as a concert hall and parliament. This structure is about 2000 years old and was destroyed in the earthquake in t
en.bodyHtml:
It is located on the upper Ephesus and built by Romans. The Odeon is well-preserved with a capacity of 1400 seats. It was used as a concert hall and parliament. This structure is about 2000 years old and was destroyed in the earthquake in the 7th Century AD.

There were vaulted gates leading to the cavea. Since there was no drainage in the orchestra, it is believed that this structure had a wooden roof. During excavations they found a marble head of the god Eros. There was stage and a stage building which was two storey. Statues of Ephesian donators were situated in the niches. Today some events are organized in this Odeon.

en.title: Latrina
en.description: These were the only public toilets in Ephesus and it is said that they were for man. Toilets are very well protected. There should be another public toilet for women in Ephesus which hasn't been found yet. There were 44 holes on the three s
en.bodyHtml:
These were the only public toilets in Ephesus and it is said that they were for man. Toilets are very well protected. There should be another public toilet for women in Ephesus which hasn't been found yet. There were 44 holes on the three sides of Ephesus.

There was a fresh water channel just in front of the holes. There were mosaic paved floors. There was an open-air pool in the center. People had to pay entrance fees to the public toilets.

en.title: Islamic Tours
en.description: Turkey is one of the countries where religions meet and the history of religions shaped. Muslims, Christians, Jews, Yezidis, Assyrians and Zoroastrians can take the traces of religion in Turkey. It is a Muslim country in which the Turkish p
en.bodyHtml:
Turkey is one of the countries where religions meet and the history of religions shaped.  Muslims, Christians, Jews, Yezidis, Assyrians and Zoroastrians can take the traces of religion in Turkey. It is a Muslim country in which the Turkish people have, throughout their history, done so much in the name of Islam, to lay the foundations with which to advance the religion and its members. They expected no reward other than the pleasure of Allah.

Urfa is a city known as “The City of Prophets” since it is where Abraham, Lot, Daniel and many others came from. Konya is the center of The Mevlevis where the great master Mevlana Celaleddin Rumi taught all his life and where he and his family are all buried. Once it was also the capital of the Seljuk Turks.

Turkey, is located close to Islam's most important centers of the Mecca, Medina and Jerusalem. 
For Islam’s Prophet Muhammed’s (sav) friends one of the closest places to spread Islam was Anatolia. That's why the very early traces of Islam seen in Turkey. However, the establishment of Islam and the most important works that were made in Turkey, begins on the 10th and 11th anniversary when Turks settled in Anatolia. Therefore there are 1.000 year old Mosques and Masjids in Anatolia. The most brilliant period of Islamic architecture was in Selcuklu and Ottoman periods. Today there are thousands of Turkish-Islamic works from one side of Anatolia, to Turkey's west part. Mosques, masjids, caravanserais, baths, madrasahs were built in the last 1000 years.

Undoubtedly, Istanbul is a summit in the history and architecture of Islam as the Ottoman Capital and the most important works are gathered here. The cities of Bursa and Edirne are also the places where Ottoman architecture is best represented.

In our Islamic Tours in Turkey you will have chance to see the most important Turkish-Islamic monuments in Turkey will be able to tour. We can prepare tailor made and customized tours for you, depending on your time and interest. We provide and private customized Islamic tours for short or large groups. Please contact us for your requests and more information.

en.bodyHtml:
We organize Persian Empire and Zoroastrian Tours in Turkey. As a tour company, want the recognition of this important civilization that left its mark in Anatolia and Zoroastrians have chance to visit this ancient civilization and culture in Turkey. As a result you will have opportunity to see both the most beautiful places in Turkey and the traces left by the Persians 2,500 years ago as well.

Zoroastrian religion was an old and official religion of the Persian Empire before Islam. Persians governed in Turkey for 200 years (BC 6 and 4th century). They fought with Greeks, Romans and Byzantines throughout history. The famous Persian kings Xerxes, Darius, Cyrus were in Anatolia. 
Ancient Sardes (present-day Salihli) in the Aegean region has been the center of their Satrap. This time of the Persian kingdom for 200 years although not much but still significant traces can be seen in today's Turkey.

There are not many Persian Empire and Zoroastrian Tours in Turkey organized. As a result you will have opportunity to see both the most beautiful places in Turkey and the traces left by the Persians 2,500 years ago as well.

en.title: Sagalassos Tours
en.description: Sagalassos is a newly discovered ancient city which attracts many archeology lovers from all over the world. Since it was just discovered 30 years ago and was lost and not known by people, neither in the past and nor in the present time it
en.bodyHtml: Sagalassos is a newly discovered ancient city which attracts many archeology lovers from all over the world. Since it was just discovered 30 years ago and was lost and not known by people, neither in the past and nor in the present time it was excavated or plundered. This gives archeologists the chance to explore a city which was not touched before. Sagalassos was just hidden on the Taurus Mountain, 1400m higher than the sea level, surrounded by a wonderful landscape. We will arrange your Sagalassos tours and you will have chance to visit this magnificent city by a professional tour guide. We offer Sagalassos day tours or tours with one day accommodation from any destination in Turkey. We will organize your flights, transfers, accommodation and private guided tour. We are also happy to customize your Sagalassos tour and combine it with other destinations such as Ephesus, Istanbul, Cappadocia if required. We can organize a Salalassos tour with an airplane connection to Sagalassos from Istanbul or Izmir. The closest airport to Sagalassos is in Isparta. Isparta airport is one hour from Sagalassos.

fr.title: Visite chrétienne
fr.description: Turkey is one of the most accurate address for Christian Tours. Turkey, which is a part of the Holy Land is a must to visit and must to see for a Christian pilgrimage. Biblical Tours in Turkey offers you many things. For example, the first
fr.bodyHtml:
Turkey is one of the most accurate address for Christian Tours. Turkey, which is a part of the Holy Land is a must to visit and must to see for a Christian pilgrimage. Biblical Tours in Turkey offers you many things. For example, the first church in the world was founded by Saint Peter in Antakya (Antioch), Turkey. Also, the first Christian communities were established in Anatolia, Turkey. 

Turkey is a true heritage for Bible readers. Many of the sites you will see once were visited by St. Paul, St. Peter (and St. John and many other disciples) where they spread the world and wrote most what we read in the Bible today.

Saint Paul was born in Tarsus city of Turkey and he wrote most of his letters in Turkey to the people of ancient cities in Turkey that these letters take part in history and Holly Bible. St. Paul did 3 missionary journeys in Turkey and travelled for 16 years. He founded a congregation in Ephesus and lived in Ephesus for two and a half years. He toured the ancient cities in Turkey and preached Christianity in synagogues and squares.

Apostle and the Evangelist Saint John, spent a large part of his life, especially in Ephesus in Turkey and even wrote his Bible in Ephesus and died in here. Today his grave in the west of Turkey near the ancient city of Ephesus. He also founded Seven Churches and his letters to these Seven Churches are included in the book of revelation. Again, Saint John brought Mother Mary to Ephesus with him and kept her with him until she died.

Turkey hosted the first Seven Ecumenical Councils. The laws that made here, influenced the Christianity throughout the history and formed the dogmas. Turkey is also one of the rare places where Jesus Christ’s native language is still spoken in a particular places. Cappadocia's three Father and many important Disciplines were born and lived in Turkey.

Our Biblical tours give you a complete study of field work as well as pleasure of being on the roads where cultures and religions meet and the living past that still lingers in the rocks of ancient sites. After following Paul and tracing early Christianity, you will have a different view and more pleasure from your Biblical readings for the rest of your life.
These tours are not only a Biblical journey but also a full exploration of the most visited parts of Turkey.

In our Christian Tours give you the chance to see and visit Christian – Biblical places in Turkey as well as the extensive history and culture. Beyond the Christian tours that we offer, we can prepare tailor made and customized Christian tours by taking you to places you want to spend most of your time or according to your time length in Turkey.

en.title: Izmir Tours
en.description: Izmir tours are one of the most beautiful and colorful tours that you can do in Turkey. We are talking about a 7000-year-old history when we call Izmir, the ancient name Smyrna. İzmir has always been an important city with its favorable wea
en.bodyHtml:
Izmir tours are one of the most beautiful and colorful tours that you can do in Turkey. We are talking about a 7000-year-old history when we call Izmir, the ancient name Smyrna. İzmir has always been an important city with its favorable weather conditions, strategic and efficient hinterland, and its diverse religious and nationality and port. Today it is the third largest city of Turkey's and the largest city in the Aegean region. Located in the Aegean Sea, this city has a population of over 3 million. This port city, has both the old city and the modern settlement, is one of Turkey's most educated and modern city. The international airport is only 20 minutes away from the city center. Izmir has a harbor for both commercial and touristic cruise ships. The International Fair has been organized for almost 50 years. Historical ruins from the ancient Greek, Roman, Selcuklu and Ottoman periods constitute the historical fabric of the city. Izmir is a very colorful city with its Archaeological and Ethnographic museum, Agora located in the Old city, Kadifekale, Smyrna Ancient City, Mosques and Inns located in the old city belong the Ottoman period. 

The possibility to go from one side to the other side of the city by ferry instead of the highway not only relieves traffic but also provides a short journey to the sea. Also metro and Izban makes it very easy to access. Thanks to Izmir airport also offers the opportunity to fly to other tourist destinations in Turkey.

We provide Izmir Tours from Your hotel, Izmir airport or port. You will be picked up by your private tour guide on the tour date. Your professional local lisenced tour guide will be together with you throughout the tour. Also private transfers and private driver will be arranged. We can provide alternative tours for you according to your request and customize an itinerary.

nl.bodyHtml:

When you do the Armenian tour, you will live the past today and maybe you will have the opportunity to see the cities and houses where your family lived for a while. Turkey, was one of the most important residential area in the history of the Armenians, and perhaps that was the most important place.

Especially in the East and South of Turkey there were many Armenian Kingdoms until 1.000 years before. The Armenians settled in all parts of Anatolia, especially in the Ottoman period, but mostly in Istanbul. Today almost everywhere in Turkey, there are works belong to Armenians. Armenians living outside of Turkey can still come and see the house where they were living 100 years ago. For sure, the most important ancient settlement of Armenians in Turkey were the Ani ruins. Visiting this ancient city gives incredible excitement.

en.title: Istanbul Tours
en.description: We organize private and customized Istanbul Tours . You can either choose one of our tours or customize your own tour. You will be guided by a professional licensed Istanbul tour guide and transported by a private, comfortable, A/C and non-
en.bodyHtml:
We organize private and customized Istanbul Tours. You can either choose one of our tours or customize your own tour. You will be guided by a professional licensed Istanbul tour guide and transported by a private, comfortable, A/C and non-smoking vehicle throughout the tour. We pick you up from the Istanbul port, airport or hotel and drop you back at the end of the tour.

Istanbul is undoubtedly one of the most interesting, largest and most special metropolises in the world. Istanbul is the only city in the world that is located on two continents. It is Turkey's largest city. It is a magnificent metropolis that has served as the capital of the Eastern Roman, Byzantine and Ottoman Empire for hundred years. Istanbul is a great brand with its history, culture, synthesis of old and new. This city, which has the best chain hotels in the world, has a modern transportation network and 3 airports. Recently, one of the world's largest and most modern airports has started to operate. You need at least one week to visit Istanbul. The most famous places to visit are the Blue Mosque, Topkapi Palace, Underground Cistern, Hagia Sofia, Grand Bazaar, Istanbul Archeology Museum and Suleymaniye Mosque, Spice Bazaar, Dolmabahce Palace, Galata Tower, Chora Church, Rüstem Pasha Mosque etc . One of the most beautiful things to do in Istanbul is Bosporus Cruise. You can see the most beautiful places of Istanbul in this tour to be made between Europe on one side and the Asian coast on the other. Flights from abroad usually come to Istanbul. There are flights from Istanbul every hour to many tourist attractions and historic cities in Turkey; such as Antalya, Cappadocia (Nevsehir-Kayseri), Izmir, Urfa, Gaziantep, Antakya, Trabzon, Van, Ankara. 

Istanbul is one of the largest and modern metropolises in the world but also a city where you can travel in history. At least one week is required to visit Istanbul. Historical and architectural mosques, churches, museums and palaces in Istanbul are numerous.

Bosporus tour, shopping in the 500-year-old bazaars, massaging in historical Turkish baths, walking on famous streets, and testing food in famous restaurants are just some of the many things you can do in Istanbul.

If you don't have a lot of time to visit Istanbul, the following tours will help you to visit the most important places within a few days, but with a private guided tour. In a private tour, you avoid unnecessary time losses and you will be able to evaluate your actual time.

We look forward to meeting you!

de.description: Are you looking for Private Ephesus Tours from Izmir ? Then, you are just at the right place. We as a recognized and recommended tour agent in Turkey, have been arranging Private Ephesus Tours since 1993 for our visitors who want to get the
de.bodyHtml:
Are you looking for Private Ephesus Tours from Izmir? Then, you are just at the right place. We as a recognized and recommended tour agent in Turkey, have been arranging Private Ephesus Tours since 1993 for our visitors who want to get the most of Ancient Ephesus. Such a tour that is meeting your expectations, requests and full of fun will be an unforgettable memory for you. We rigorously choose our Ephesus Tour guides as they have the most important role during the tour. They are all licensed, professional local guides, eager to show you the beauties and history of Ephesus and its surroundings. Our tour guides great reviews on TripAdvisor written by our visitors.

Maybe you will never have a second chance to visit Ephesus and have a limited time in the area. As a team who are aware of this, we do our best to make it a wonderful time for you. We will arrange everything for you before your arrival to Izmir port or airport. Your Ephesus Tour guide will be waiting for you at the Izmir port or airport exit gate with a big smile at the arranged time, outside the port you will meet your private driver and get on a luxurious, clean and A/C van or mini-bus that is waiting for you. You will be the only ones in your Ephesus Tour. Your guide will be together with you during your Ephesus Tour and get the tickets ready in advanced for you to save time and skip the lines. You can always ask him/her as many questions as you wish about Ephesus history, Turkey, Turkish culture, Turkish history etc. and your guide is always happy to answer them all.

Your tour guide will take you to a lovely, quiet and non-touristy local restaurant where you will have delicious lunch. You will be served starters from Turkish cuisine, BBQ and fruits. We always get great feedbacks about the lunch and the food from our visitors!

At the end of your Ephesus Tour your private tour guide and driver will drop you back to Izmir port, airport or hotel. Our aim is to make your Ephesus tour  the highlight of your entire cruise tour.

Please check out our various options of Ephesus Tours from Izmir.

As a flexible tour agent, we also offer you different tour options from Izmir for the ones who visites Ephesus before or looking for someting else. You can find our Pamukkale tours, Pergamum Tours and Seven Churches tours written below.

We look forward to meeting you and make it a MAGICAL day for you!

fr.title: Visites juives
fr.description: Judaism is one of the oldest religions in the world. In the ancient cities in Turkey, there were Jewish settlements as well as Paganism and there were defiantly synagogues in the cities. In addition to hundreds of paganism necessarily a Jew
fr.bodyHtml:
Judaism is one of the oldest religions in the world. In the ancient cities in Turkey, there were Jewish settlements as well as Paganism and there were defiantly synagogues in the cities. 

In addition to hundreds of paganism necessarily a Jewish settlement in the ancient city in Turkey and synagogues in the city has been located.  Judaism, which was the first of the Abrahamic religions, spread throughout Anatolia in ancient times. Abraham is from Urfa. Job also lived in Urfa. Apart from this, the Jews who had to flee from Spain during the Ottoman period in 1492 were welcomed and they were mostly settled in Istanbul and Izmir. Thus, important synagogues are still active in Izmir and especially in Istanbul. 

In our Jewish Tours in Turkey, there are visits to the big cities where some important Jewish settlements are located and the synagogues are still active. Please contact us for more information or your request.

ru.title: Туры в Эфес
ru.description: Welcome to our Ephesus Tours page! Ephesus Tours with different highlights and durations are prepared for you by our experienced team. We will pick you up from Kusadasi, Izmir or Istanbul port/airport/hotel. Our Ephesus tours include visits
ru.bodyHtml:
Welcome to our Ephesus Tours page!

Ephesus Tours with different highlights and durations are prepared for you by our experienced team. We will pick you up from Kusadasi, Izmir or Istanbul port/airport/hotel. Our Ephesus tours include visits to Ancient Ephesus, House of the Virgin Mary, Terrace Houses, Basilica of St. John, Artemis Temple, Sirince Village and Ephesus Museum. We are very happy to customize your Ephesus excursions according to your needs and expectations. Your Ephesus Tours can be longer, shorter or we can add different places in your tour program as you request.

You will be guided by a private professional licensed tour guide throughout your Ephesus tour and will be transferred by a private comfortable, A/C and non-smoking vehicle. Your tour guide will pick you up from Kusadasi/Izmir port or from your hotel in Kusadasi/Izmir and drop you back to at the end of your Ephesus Tour. Ephesus is only 20 mins drive from Kusadasi port. You will be transferred to Ephesus by your private driver by a luxurious and comfortable vehicle. We guarantee that you will be dropped back to Kusadasi port 45 minutes before your cruise leaves Kusadasi port.

If you let us know at the time of booking, you have the chance to have English speaking, French speaking, Spanish speaking, German speaking tour guides for your Ephesus Tours. All of our tour guides are selected carefully and they do their best to make it a great and memorable day in Ephesus. Your private local tour guide will give you most of the information during your tour. You can ask your tour guide as many questions as you wish because it is a private tour and you will be the only ones throughout your Ephesus Tours.

We will provide Ephesus tickets before your arrival and your guide will have them ready on the tour date. All the entrance fees stated in the itineraries, private guide, private transfers, parking and lunch are included in the price. There are definitely no hidden costs.

Are you in Istanbul and want to see Ephesus for one day? Then, we will pick you up from your hotel in Istanbul and provide you with a full day private Ephesus Tours from Istanbul.

We are very proud to arrange Ephesus Tours as a local tour company established in 1993, Kusadasi Turkey. Magical Steps Tours deserved the Certificates of Excellence in 2012, 2013, 2014, 2015, 2016 and 2017. Please visit our TripAdvisor page for our reviews written by our visitors who booked their Ephesus excursions with us. tr.title: Türkiye kültür
tr.description: Turkey is considered to be the gateway between East and West , due to its historical, geographical and cultural position. Living here in Turkey we know that our country attracts the attention of the rest of the world. Our society readily us
tr.bodyHtml:
Turkey is considered to be the gateway between East and West, due to its historical, geographical and cultural position. Living here in Turkey we know that our country attracts the attention of the rest of the world. Our society readily uses its historical and cultural legacy to facilitate intercultural dialog. Consequently our perspective is devoted to Turkey's own historical and cultural significance, our society's secular nature means that we are always open to the study of interreligious affairs.

Turkey has the biggest area compared to the other countries in Europe. Three sides are surrounded by the sea which makes the land look like a natural peninsula.

It has a very strategic places being in the bridge between Europe and Asia and neighbors to many important locations. On the one hand and incredible diversity occurs by the Aegean, the Balkans, the Black Sea, Mediterranean and Caucasus. At the same time it is the center of the old world. It hosted the most important civilizations and the birth place of the religions.

When we consider Turkey Tours, we don’t mean one specific place or time. In Turkey Tours we invite you to explore and visit 12000 years of recorded history, many civilizations, hundreds of ancient cities, nature beauties, the centers of the oldest religions, incredible beaches, hundreds of high quality hotels high rated in the world and meet the most hospitable people in the world.

To describe our interest in interreligious dialogue and our approach to the tours that we provide, we aim to educate people about Turkey's historical background. The tours and their diversity mean that you can examine the factors influencing all of the Abrahamic religions regardless of whether you belong to any one religion or cultural group.

7 regions of Turkey have the most importance for tourism. We prepared various Turkey Tours itineraries for you including different regions and periods. Our Turkey tours also include religious tours. We have Christian Tours, Jewish Tours, Islamic Tours and Zoroastrian Tours.

Cappadocia Tours are also included in our Turkey Tours. We organize cave hotel bookings, flights, transfers, Daily Cappadocia Tours and hot air balloon rides. You can also find Anzac Tour itineraries in our website. We arrange these tours all year round 3.

As an experienced and recommended travel agent, we will do our best to answer your expectations and make your Turkey Tours a life time memory. We will arrange your hotel booking, book a professional experienced tour guide, hotel and airport transfers, and domestic flights for you. According you your duration, expectations, interests and needs we will suggest the best itinerary for you.

Magical Steps Travel has received TripAdvisor Excellence Certificate for the last 5 years. Please visit our TripAdvisor page to read the reviews we received from our customers who used our services. Customer satisfaction is our number one and our team work hard to spend your time in Turkey in the best way. We choose the best tour guides for you who are professional, well-educated and have a sense of humor.

We look forward to meeting you in Turkey.

Turkey Tours Information

Which is the best airport in Turkey to land in first?

International Flights are mostly landing in Istanbul Ataturk International Airport. Also there is another airport in Istanbul called Sabiha Gokcen.

Are there any other International Airports in Turkey?

You can also arrive in Ankara and Izmir Airports.

How can I get my Turkish visa?

You can get it easily and quickly for 20USD at the customs at the Airports or the Ports in Turkey. If you are a cruiser, mostly the cruise companies get the visa for its cruisers.

What if my Turkey Tour doesn’t start in Istanbul?

From Istanbul, Ankara and Izmir airports there are many domestic flights to all other airports in Turkey. So you can get easily access to other airports and cities.

Should I prefer to travel by plane for my Turkey Tours?

Flying is the easiest way and is not expensive in Turkey. But you may also use high-speed trains, ferryboats and comfortable busses and vans.

How can I book my Turkey Tour?

There are various itineraries in our website including cultural tours, religious tours, combined tours, Istanbul, Ephesus and Cappadocia tours. We also customize tours for you according to your requests, needs and expectations.

How does a customized tour work?

You can make a list of the places that you wish to visit in Turkey. We will make the best itinerary and pricing for you.

What kind of services do you provide in Turkey tours?

We will provide the whole services for you including your international flight to and from Turkey, domestic flights, airport and hotel transfers, all the hotel bookings, professional tour guiding, meals, tours, entrance fees and the obligatory travel insurance. (You should get your international travel insurance at your country.)

Can I choose my hotels?

Yes, we can send a selection of hotels for you to choose or you can search on the internet and we will get the best price and book your hotels.

When is the best time for Turkey Tours?

Turkey can be visited all year round. If your aim is to travel and see many places, then we would suggest to so your Turkey tour either in spring or autumn. If you wish to swim and be close to the seaside, then the best months are May, June July, August, September and October.

If I wish to travel Turkey by cruise, which places have cruise ports?

We can provide tour services from most of the cruise ports. The most popular cruise ports are in Istanbul, Kusadasi (Ephesus), Izmir, Bodrum and Antalya. There are also ports in Dikili, Alanya, Trabzon, Samsun and Sinop.

Do I need to have Turkish Lira with me during my stay in Turkey?

No, the reason these areas are touristic places, you can make payments in USD, Euro or by Credit Card. You can also make the tour payment in USD or Euro. Also there are many ATM’s for you to easily get Turkish Lira. Your tour guide will help you with it.

Which parts of Turkey is ideal to visit in which months?

Western Seacoast of Turkey has ideal weather conditions for tourism. So the Aegean, Mediterranean and Marmara regions are suitable to visit all year round. Black Sea, Middle Anatolia and Eastern Turkey can be snowy in winter. You can visit Turkey in spring, summer and autumn.

How is the quality of the hotels in Turkey?

The capacity of the hotels is available for 50 million tourists to accommodate. Various categories of accommodation exist. There are famous world hotel brands and most of the hotels serve in high quality and listed in the top in worldwide.

How is the quality of transportation in Turkey?

In recent years sea, motorways and train transportation has developed a lot. Tunnels and bridges are built in many cities. The busses used in tourism and domestic transfers are very comfortable and new. 26 new airports were built in last 12 years and nearly every city has an airport in Turkey. There are many flight companies which provide good prices and high quality.

How is the health system and hospitals in Turkey?

Turkey has the best health system after the last reforms. Many government and private hospitals were built in recent years. Even people from the most developed countries come to Turkey to get health service. As a tourist visiting Turkey, you can always get a health service. If you have insurance you can get any kind of health services.

Do the tour guides have a certificate in Turkey?

Turkish government gives a big importance to tourism and the tourists. The most important person introducing the country is the tour guide. All the tour guides are educated and finish tour guiding branch at university. And have the certificate for the language that you will be a tour guide. It is a professional job in Turkey.

Which are the most popular destinations in Turkey?

Turkey is a cradle of civilizations and hosted many different nations because of its strategic situation and size. You will be able to see these in our Turkey tours; Ruins from Haitian, Urartian, Frig, Lydian, Asuri Colonies, Greek Civilization, Roman, Lycian, Byzantium, Seljukian and Ottoman times. The most tourist destinations in Turkey are Istanbul, Antalya, Cappadocia, Gobeklitepe, Izmir, Ephesus, Marmaris, Bodrum, Fethiye, Bergama, Gallipoli, Troy, Pamukkale and Bursa.

Why Turkey is important for the early Christianity?

Turkey is the place called Holly Land. This area is not important only for Christianity but also for the other religions. The first church ever built is in Antioch (Antakya). Turkey is where St. Paul was born and lived. His missionary journey which took 16 years was in Turkey. He stayed in Ephesus for 2 and half years. It is also known that Maria Magdalena, St Lukas, Virgin Mary and St. John (the Evangelist) died in Turkey. St John wrote the Gospel, St Luke wrote the Book of Acts and St. Paul wrote his famous letters in Turkey.

The 7 Churches that St John established and wrote in the Book of Revolution are in Turkey. They are Philadelphia, Sardis, Ephesus, Pergamum, Thyatira, Laodicea and Smyrna. Turkey is also hosted the 7 Ecumenical Council. St. Tecla, St. Basil and 2 famous St. George (father of Cappadocia) was in Turkey. There are also many symbolic historical places in Turkey such as Hagia Sophia. You can visit all of these places in your Turkey Tours.

How to shop in Turkey and how to make a payment?

You can find any kind of products in Turkey; the most modern, popular brands and traditional things in the old bazars. Grand Bazar and Spice Bazaar are very historical places in Istanbul. The most popular historical products are carpet, kelim, ceramic, clay, gold, silver and copper products. Also leather and textile are very important. Turkish deserts are very famous as well. Turkish delight with nuts are very good gift to buy for your friends.

Fashion week and shopping evets – organizations are held in Istanbul.

Turkish currency is Turkish Lira but many different currencies are accepted in Tourist destinations. You can also use your credit card.

You can make a list of the places that you wish to visit in Turkey. We will make the best itinerary and pricing for you.

What kind of services do you provide in Turkey tours?

We will provide the whole services for you including your international flight to and from Turkey, domestic flights, airport and hotel transfers, all the hotel bookings, professional tour guiding, meals, tours, entrance fees and the obligatory travel insurance. (You should get your international travel insurance at your country.)

Can I choose my hotels?

Yes, we can send a selection of hotels for you to choose or you can search on the internet and we will get the best price and book your hotels.

When is the best time for Turkey Tours?

Turkey can be visited all year round. If your aim is to travel and see many places, then we would suggest to so your Turkey tour either in spring or autumn. If you wish to swim and be close to the seaside, then the best months are May, June July, August, September and October.

If I wish to travel Turkey by cruise, which places have cruise ports?

We can provide tour services from most of the cruise ports. The most popular cruise ports are in Istanbul, Kusadasi (Ephesus), Izmir, Bodrum and Antalya. There are also ports in Dikili, Alanya, Trabzon, Samsun and Sinop.

Do I need to have Turkish Lira with me during my stay in Turkey?

No, the reason these areas are touristic places, you can make payments in USD, Euro or by Credit Card. You can also make the tour payment in USD or Euro. Also there are many ATM’s for you to easily get Turkish Lira. Your tour guide will help you with it.

Which parts of Turkey is ideal to visit in which months?

Western Seacoast of Turkey has ideal weather conditions for tourism. So the Aegean, Mediterranean and Marmara regions are suitable to visit all year round. Black Sea, Middle Anatolia and Eastern Turkey can be snowy in winter. You can visit Turkey in spring, summer and autumn.

How is the quality of the hotels in Turkey?

The capacity of the hotels is available for 50 million tourists to accommodate. Various categories of accommodation exist. There are famous world hotel brands and most of the hotels serve in high quality and listed in the top in worldwide.

How is the quality of transportation in Turkey?

In recent years sea, motorways and train transportation has developed a lot. Tunnels and bridges are built in many cities. The busses used in tourism and domestic transfers are very comfortable and new. 26 new airports were built in last 12 years and nearly every city has an airport in Turkey. There are many flight companies which provide good prices and high quality.

How is the health system and hospitals in Turkey?

Turkey has the best health system after the last reforms. Many government and private hospitals were built in recent years. Even people from the most developed countries come to Turkey to get health service. As a tourist visiting Turkey, you can always get a health service. If you have insurance you can get any kind of health services.

Do the tour guides have a certificate in Turkey?

Turkish government gives a big importance to tourism and the tourists. The most important person introducing the country is the tour guide. All the tour guides are educated and finish tour guiding branch at university. And have the certificate for the language that you will be a tour guide. It is a professional job in Turkey.

Which are the most popular destinations in Turkey?

Turkey is a cradle of civilizations and hosted many different nations because of its strategic situation and size. You will be able to see these in our Turkey tours; Ruins from Haitian, Urartian, Frig, Lydian, Asuri Colonies, Greek Civilization, Roman, Lycian, Byzantium, Seljukian and Ottoman times. The most tourist destinations in Turkey are Istanbul, Antalya, Cappadocia, Gobeklitepe, Izmir, Ephesus, Marmaris, Bodrum, Fethiye, Bergama, Gallipoli, Troy, Pamukkale and Bursa.

Why Turkey is important for the early Christianity?

Turkey is the place called Holly Land. This area is not important only for Christianity but also for the other religions. The first church ever built is in Antioch (Antakya). Turkey is where St. Paul was born and lived. His missionary journey which took 16 years was in Turkey. He stayed in Ephesus for 2 and half years. It is also known that Maria Magdalena, St Lukas, Virgin Mary and St. John (the Evangelist) died in Turkey. St John wrote the Gospel, St Luke wrote the Book of Acts and St. Paul wrote his famous letters in Turkey.

The 7 Churches that St John established and wrote in the Book of Revolution are in Turkey. They are Philadelphia, Sardis, Ephesus, Pergamum, Thyatira, Laodicea and Smyrna. Turkey is also hosted the 7 Ecumenical Council. St. Tecla, St. Basil and 2 famous St. George (father of Cappadocia) was in Turkey. There are also many symbolic historical places in Turkey such as Hagia Sophia. You can visit all of these places in your Turkey Tours.

How to shop in Turkey and how to make a payment?

You can find any kind of products in Turkey; the most modern, popular brands and traditional things in the old bazars. Grand Bazar and Spice Bazaar are very historical places in Istanbul. The most popular historical products are carpet, kelim, ceramic, clay, gold, silver and copper products. Also leather and textile are very important. Turkish deserts are very famous as well. Turkish delight with nuts are very good gift to buy for your friends.

Fashion week and shopping evets – organizations are held in Istanbul.

Turkish currency is Turkish Lira but many different currencies are accepted in Tourist destinations. You can also use your credit card.

en.bodyHtml:
Turkey is considered to be the gateway between East and West, due to its historical, geographical and cultural position. Living here in Turkey we know that our country attracts the attention of the rest of the world. Our society readily uses its historical and cultural legacy to facilitate intercultural dialog. Consequently our perspective is devoted to Turkey's own historical and cultural significance, our society's secular nature means that we are always open to the study of interreligious affairs.

Turkey has the biggest area compared to the other countries in Europe. Three sides are surrounded by the sea which makes the land look like a natural peninsula.

It has a very strategic places being in the bridge between Europe and Asia and neighbors to many important locations. On the one hand and incredible diversity occurs by the Aegean, the Balkans, the Black Sea, Mediterranean and Caucasus. At the same time it is the center of the old world. It hosted the most important civilizations and the birth place of the religions.

When we consider Turkey Tours, we don’t mean one specific place or time. In Turkey Tours we invite you to explore and visit 12000 years of recorded history, many civilizations, hundreds of ancient cities, nature beauties, the centers of the oldest religions, incredible beaches, hundreds of high quality hotels high rated in the world and meet the most hospitable people in the world.

To describe our interest in interreligious dialogue and our approach to the tours that we provide, we aim to educate people about Turkey's historical background. The tours and their diversity mean that you can examine the factors influencing all of the Abrahamic religions regardless of whether you belong to any one religion or cultural group.

7 regions of Turkey have the most importance for tourism. We prepared various Turkey Tours itineraries for you including different regions and periods. Our Turkey tours also include religious tours. We have Christian Tours, Jewish Tours, Islamic Tours and Zoroastrian Tours.

We will arrange your hotel booking, book a professional experienced tour guide, hotel and airport transfers, and domestic flights for you. According you your duration, expectations, interests and needs we will suggest the best itinerary for you.

Magical Steps Travel has received TripAdvisor Excellence Certificate for the last 5 years. Please visit our TripAdvisor page to read the reviews we received from our customers who used our services. Customer satisfaction is our number one and our team work hard to spend your time in Turkey in the best way. We choose the best tour guides for you who are professional, well-educated and have a sense of humor.

We look forward to meeting you in Turkey.

en.title: Cappadocia Tours
en.description: Cappadocia is a unique place in the world where you can feel yourself out of this world for a few days. Cappadocia meaning of the word 'Beautiful Country of Horses'. Cappadocia is located in the crossroads of the four cities in the middle o
en.bodyHtml:
Cappadocia is a unique place in the world where you can feel yourself out of this world for a few days. Cappadocia meaning of the word 'Beautiful Country of Horses'. Cappadocia is located in the crossroads of the four cities in the middle of Turkey. These are Kayseri, Nigde, Aksaray and Nevsehir. The most famous settlements in Cappadocia are Goreme, Urgup and Avanos.

Cappadocia is a large area consisting of fairy chimneys, valleys, hills and underground cities formed by the eruption of volcanic mountains and lava that were once active here thousands of years ago and these lavas were eroded by rain and wind in thousands of years. Cappadocia is really a fairytale place. However, the only feature is not the fairy chimneys of nature. At the same time as it is anywhere in Turkey, where you'll find the traces of the civilization of mankind is a history of thousands of years. This is a long-standing settlement starting from the Hittites. It is also important in terms of early and late Christianity. Numerous fairy chimney churches and enormous icon and fresco ornaments in Cappadocia.

Thousands of people were able to hide at the same time in Derinkuyu and Kaymakli Underground Cities for hundreds of years. Our aim is to show you all the most important places of Cappadocia with comfortable private or semi-private tours in a short time. In addition to Cappadocia tours, you will enjoy this fairytale place with hot air balloon rides, horse riding and other activities. Cappadocia is a place that offers a boutique hotel concept unlike other destinations. This is a place where you can stay in the original cave and cut stone hotels with amazing views.

You will have chance to explore all Cappadocia in 3 or 5 days. You can choose the best itinerary for you and you can also customize your own tour. We will pick you up from anywhere in Turkey and arrange your airport transfers, Cappadocia flights and return, Cappadocia tours by a professinal tour guides and hotel in Cappadocia.

Please also check our combined Cappadocia and Ephesus Tours and Cappadocia Istanbul Ephesus Tours 

We look forward to meeting you.

reviews.name: Wilma Mortimer
reviews.text: Today we had a tour of Ephesus. The driver was punctual and polite. The car was very clear. As we were 4 women travelling we felt very safe. The guide Atilla was most kind + informative. We enjoyed his company immensely. We would highly recommend both driver and guide.

reviews.name: Debbie Couch
reviews.text: This was a wonderful excursion. It was my favorite from my entire cruise. The driver did a great job and the guide Volkan was excellent, very personable and spoke perfect English. It was also very informative. I learned a lot about the Turkish culture as well as the wonderful sites we visited. The vehicle was great and the food was also. Thank you so much! I hope to return soon to take another wonderful tour with your company.
